Title: GRIN2B encephalopathy: novel findings on phenotype, variant clustering, functional consequences and treatment aspects.
Authors: Konrad Platzer; Hongjie Yuan; Hannah Schütz; Alexander Winschel; Wenjuan Chen; Chun Hu; Hirofumi Kusumoto; Henrike O Heyne; Katherine L Helbig; Sha Tang; Marcia C Willing; Brad T Tinkle; Darius J Adams; Christel Depienne; Boris Keren; Cyril Mignot; Eirik Frengen; Petter Strømme; Saskia Biskup; Dennis Döcker; Tim M Strom; Heather C Mefford; Candace T Myers; Alison M Muir; Amy LaCroix; Lynette Sadleir; Ingrid E Scheffer; Eva Brilstra; Mieke M van Haelst; Jasper J van der Smagt; Levinus A Bok; Rikke S Møller; Uffe B Jensen; John J Millichap; Anne T Berg; Ethan M Goldberg; Isabelle De Bie; Stephanie Fox; Philippe Major; Julie R Jones; Elaine H Zackai; Rami Abou Jamra; Arndt Rolfs; Richard J Leventer; John A Lawson; Tony Roscioli; Floor E Jansen; Emmanuelle Ranza; Christian M Korff; Anna-Elina Lehesjoki; Carolina Courage; Tarja Linnankivi; Douglas R Smith; Christine Stanley; Mark Mintz; Dianalee McKnight; Amy Decker; Wen-Hann Tan; Mark A Tarnopolsky; Lauren I Brady; Markus Wolff; Lutz Dondit; Helio F Pedro; Sarah E Parisotto; Kelly L Jones; Anup D Patel; David N Franz; Rena Vanzo; Elysa Marco; Judith D Ranells; Nataliya Di Donato; William B Dobyns; Bodo Laube; Stephen F Traynelis; Johannes R Lemke
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed for a comprehensive delineation of genetic, functional and phenotypic aspects of GRIN2B encephalopathy and explored potential prospects of personalised medicine.
METHODS: Data of 48 individuals with de novo GRIN2B variants were collected from several diagnostic and research cohorts, as well as from 43 patients from the literature. Functional consequences and response to memantine treatment were investigated in vitro and eventually translated into patient care.
RESULTS: Overall, de novo variants in 86 patients were classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic. Patients presented with neurodevelopmental disorders and a spectrum of hypotonia, movement disorder, cortical visual impairment, cerebral volume loss and epilepsy. Six patients presented with a consistent malformation of cortical development (MCD) intermediate between tubulinopathies and polymicrogyria. Missense variants cluster in transmembrane segments and ligand-binding sites. Functional consequences of variants were diverse, revealing various potential gain-of-function and loss-of-function mechanisms and a retained sensitivity to the use-dependent blocker memantine. However, an objectifiable beneficial treatment response in the respective patients still remains to be demonstrated.
CONCLUSIONS: In addition to previously known features of intellectual disability, epilepsy and autism, we found evidence that GRIN2B encephalopathy is also frequently associated with movement disorder, cortical visual impairment and MCD revealing novel phenotypic consequences of channelopathies.

The paper never states that the 86 patients all had GRIN2B variants in that sentence; this is inferred from context. The sentence also does not report an association between a Disease entity (GRIN2B encephalopathy) and a Gene (GRIN2B) as ASSOCIATED_WITH. The 86 figure also mixes the 48 new and 43 literature patients (91 total), which means the number is not fully traceable to the stated context. Ambiguity means the claim fails.

rejected.reason: The candidate says the study looked at people with GRIN2B encephalopathy, described as a brain condition linked to changes in the GRIN2B gene. The cited claims (C1, C4) only support Disease->Phenotype relations: GRIN2B encephalopathy is associated with movement disorder, and patients presented with hypotonia and other features. Neither claim, nor its quoted evidence, states that the condition is linked to GRIN2B gene changes or describes it as a brain condition. The quotes mention "de novo GRIN2B variants" only in the study_context metadata, not in a cited relation. The gene-link clause is therefore an unsupported plain-language explanation added by the candidate. The population framing (people with GRIN2B encephalopathy) is partly supported by the cohort context, but the study design (48 individuals with de novo variants plus 43 literature patients) is omitted. The summary's key clauses are not backed by the cited claims, so it fails.

summary.text: The study included 48 people with new (de novo) GRIN2B variants, plus 43 patients taken from earlier published reports.

rejected.reason: The candidate sentence is a description of cohort composition (48 de novo GRIN2B individuals plus 43 literature patients). The cited claims, C1 and C2, assert something different: that GRIN2B encephalopathy is frequently associated with movement disorder and cortical visual impairment. The quoted evidence for both claims contains only that association statement, with no counts. The cohort numbers appear only in the study_context metadata, which is not source evidence for the quote. Neither claim's quote verifies the 48 and 43 figures, the 'de novo' status of the 48, or the origin of the 43 patients in earlier published reports. Neither claim states a cohort-composition relation, so the cited claims do not support the sentence. In addition, C1's context notes that 86 were classified pathogenic/likely pathogenic. The candidate omits this, so it may imply that all 91 individuals carry confirmed pathogenic variants. The sentence therefore cannot be verified against the cited claims and their evidence.

rejected.reason: The candidate is a meta-statement that the abstract gave no exact frequencies and that results are associations only. The first part is partly supported by the claims' limitations: C1, C2, C4 and C5 each note that frequency is not quantified in the abstract. The second part is not supported for all cited claims. C4 and C5 are descriptive observations of presenting phenotypes ("patients presented with..."), not stated associations. Calling them "associations only" adds an interpretation that the source does not make. The candidate also says "these features" without naming them. It does not distinguish between claims that say "frequently associated" (C1, C2) and claims that only say patients presented with a spectrum (C4, C5). "Frequently associated" in C1 and C2 implies a qualitative frequency, so "did not give exact frequencies" is acceptable there, but the blanket "associations only" framing is not directly stated in the source. The sentence also adds a causation-versus-association caveat that is not in the cited evidence. The unresolved canonical IDs are not a problem on their own. Because of the ambiguous scope and the unsupported "associations only" generalization, the candidate fails.
